entries.title: What is phishing?
entries.answer: Phishing is a trick where someone makes a message look trustworthy to get you to give them something or do something. They might ask for a password, send a link that leads to a fake sign-in page, or try to get you to open a file. Some messages pretend to be from a familiar game or website. If a message surprises you or asks you to rush, stop before you tap anything. Show it to a trusted grown-up who can help check where it came from.
facts: A message can have a familiar logo and still be fake.
An unexpected request for a password is a reason to pause and ask for help.

entries.title: Why do you need a password?
entries.answer: A password is a secret you enter to help show you are allowed to sign in to an account. If someone else learns it, they may be able to sign in as you. A long password that is hard to guess helps protect the account. Using a different one on each account helps too. Then learning one password does not give someone the same secret for all your accounts. If you are setting up an account, a trusted grown-up can help you choose a password and a safe way to keep it.
facts: A familiar pet name by itself can be easy to guess.
A password manager can remember different passwords with help from its owner.
